correctness.rationale: PASS: The claimed finite domain is exactly simple wheels C_r*K_1 for 3≤r≤10 with both orientations of each undirected edge, no loops and F2 reduced simplicial homology. A face is exactly an indegree/outdegree ≤1 acyclic selected arc subset: directed paths cannot branch or cycle; conversely such a finite directed graph decomposes into disjoint directed paths. The source checker uses complete inclusion/exclusion through all 4r arc labels and an independent orientation of undirected degree≤2 acyclic path forests; both enumerate all faces. A freshly written independent third implementation used undirected path-forest union-find enumeration and consistent two-way orientations, then formed every simplicial boundary column and reduced by exact bitwise F2 Gaussian elimination for each r=3..10. All face counts, chain dimensions, ranks, connectedness and Euler–Poincaré identities matched the source log and claims; at r=10: 220395 faces including empty, chain dimensions (40,610,4660,19720,47964,67160,52900,22360,4620,360), positive boundary ranks (39,571,4089,15631,32333,34778,18082,4238,340). β_d=dim C_d−rank ∂_d−rank ∂_{d+1}, with β_0=1, yields reduced F2 ranks 49,40,40,42,20 at degrees 5..9 and zero elsewhere. Previous seven r have at most four nonzero reduced degrees. These are exhaustive finite computations within the declared domain, not extrapolations to r>10, integral torsion or homotopy.

Known bidirectional-polygon homology treats a rim lacking the hub; the all-parameter bidirected double-star theorem concerns trees; same-wheel discrete-Morse results compute a different complex; general cone/quiver statements do not give the F2 ranks. value.rationale: PASS: The wheel C_r*K_1 is the canonical first hub augmentation of a polygon, and the multipath complex measures topology of disjoint directed path selections. The exact eight-case homology census, including the first case with five separate nonzero degrees, supplies reproducible and potentially useful benchmark data for understanding spoke-induced homology; its four lower ranks at r=10 are not mechanically determined by the known top-rank theorem or the polygon result. The full 220395-face computation is substantial, not a tiny check. This is a motivated finite cutoff for a natural family, without falsely asserting an all-wheel classification, infinite monotonicity, integral torsion or a new top-rank result.

final_claim: For 3≤r≤10, on the fully bidirected wheel W_{r+1}=C_r*K_1 with 4r labeled arcs, the reduced multipath-complex homology over F2 has nonzero Betti dictionaries: r=3 {1:7,2:6}; 4 {2:19,3:8}; 5 {2:2,3:23,4:10}; 6 {3:29,4:26,5:12}; 7 {4:43,5:30,6:14}; 8 {4:37,5:32,6:34,7:16}; 9 {5:71,6:36,7:38,8:18}; 10 {5:49,6:40,7:40,8:42,9:20}; all other reduced F2 Betti numbers vanish within the stated cases. Consequently r=10 is the first simple wheel in this ordered family with five nonzero reduced homology degrees. No assertion for larger wheels, integral torsion, or full homotopy type.
limitations: This is an exact exhaustive finite range r=3..10 over the coefficient field F2; it does not prove statements for r>10, integral torsion, or homotopy type.
The boundary-rank elimination and two graph face algorithms are fully exhaustive for the stated eight cases, not a surrogate for an infinite-family proof.
Originality is best-of-knowledge qualified: a prior unindexed wheel table or an unexpectedly stronger universal theorem might imply the result; highest-degree rank 2r was already known.

Publication-plan readiness is staging of two exact privacy-sanitized metadata replacements, not a GitHub write, external certification or server intake. Formal Lean/expert verification channels remain unchanged.
